sonnet.problem: Most of the stop's choice cards are pure recall of names or places that the earlier cards never set up, so a baker can only guess. Card 4 asks for Haran's son, card 6 for Abram's wife, card 7 for Milcah's father, card 10 for the destination Canaan, and card 12 for where the family settles. Card 8 is also a surprise (Abram and Sarai have no children) that the setup points the other way on. Only card 11 can be reasoned out. The story cards give no context that would let a thoughtful baker reason to these answers.
sonnet.rule: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.
